1. By way of the present application filed by Smt. Heera Devi (hereinafter referred as ''the aggrieved'') under Section 12 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 against her husband Sh. Bhagwan Dass (hereinafter referred as "the respondent"), the aggrieved has CC No:
189/1 Smt. Heera Devi Vs. Sh. Bhagwan Dass Page No. 1 of 12 sought Protection orders under Section 18; Residence Order under Section 19; Monetary Relief under Section 20; and compensation/ damages under Section 22 of the Act.

entities.text: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
entities.label: STATUTE

entities.text: Heera Devi Vs. Sh. Bhagwan Dass
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is pertinent to note that summoning qua the respondent no.2 and respondent no.3 was declined by the Ld Predecessor court vide orders dated 06.11.2013 and 11.07.2014 respectively.

2. Briefly stated, it is the grievance of the aggrieved that she got married to respondent no.1 long ago as per Hindu rites and customs but respondent no. 1 was indifferent, cruel and hostile towards the aggrieved since beginning and being a habitual drunkard, various cruelties, harassment, atrocities,
Cc No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi vs . Sh. Bhagwan Dass Page No. 1 Of 12 on 31 August, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62375663/
1 humiliation, maltreatment, ill treatment, taunting, abuses, beatings and threats to the aggrieved were extended by the respondent which she tolerated in the hope that respondent will mend his ways with the passage of time but to no avail.

It is further averred by the aggrieved that even the respondent no. 2 in connivance and collusion with the respondent no. 1 started harassing,
humiliating, torturing, abusing and beating the aggrieved as well as her younger daughter Manju.
It is further averred that respondent no. 2 even got married to respondent no.3 without permission of the aggrieved/other family members but subsequently the said marriage was accepted.
3. It is further averred that the respondent no. 2 at the instigation and in collusion with respondent no. 3 started harassing, humiliating and torturing and aggrieved as well as her daughter Manju.

It is further averred that daughter of aggrieved Manju lodged a complaint with CC No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi Vs. Sh. Bhagwan Dass Page No. 2 of 12 SHO, PS Ambedkar Nagar on 15.10.2013 vide DD No.
49B with respect to the cruelties, harassment, maltreatment, atrocities meted out to her as well as the aggrieved at the hands of the respondent no. 1, 2 and 3.
4.

entities.text: CC No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi Vs. Sh. Bhagwan Dass Page No. 2 of 12
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also averred that the respondent no. 2 and 3 even after their marriage, frequently visited the house of the aggrieved, used to stay there most of the times and instigated and induced the respondent no. 1 against the aggrieved and Manju and that as and when they visited, they stole costly belongings/household articles from the house and upon protest by the aggrieved, they quarreled with her and also abused her.

It is also averred that on 18.10.2013 at night, the aggrieved found some articles were again stolen by respondent no. 2 and 3 and lodged a complaint with SHO,
P.S. Ambedkar Nagar on 18.10.2013.

5. It is also the grievance of the aggrieved that she was the owner of a property measuring 100 sq yards, at Narela, New Delhi, which the respondents sold fraudulently in connivance and collusion with each other without her knowledge and permission for a sale consideration amount of Rs.
15,00,000/ which said amount was not given to the aggrieved.

It is also averred that the respondents have also harassed the aggrieved and Manju and asked her to vacate the house and they also threatened the aggrieved to dispossess her from the house forcefully if she fails to vacate the house.

6. It is also averred that on 26.10.2013 at about 11.30 am, the respondents in connivance and collusion with each other, forcefully entered into the ground floor of the house where the aggrieved was residing alongwith CC No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi Vs. Sh. Bhagwan Dass Page No. 3 of 12 Manju and started abusing and assaulting the aggrieved and Manju mercilessly and thereafter they forcefully threw them out from the ground floor of the house and that the respondents without having any rights, want to sell and create third party interest in the house after forcefully dispossessing the aggrieved and Manju from the house.
7.

entities.text: Heera Devi Vs. Sh. Bhagwan Dass
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is averred that the aggrieved is presently residing on the top floor of the house under the tin shed alongwith Manju and the respondents have not allowed them to use necessary amenities i.e.
bathroom, toilet and to go down stairs and go outside the house for necessary requirement and the respondents have not provided the maintenance and proper food to the aggrieved and Manju.

It is further averred that the respondent no. 1 never cared nor provided any maintenance to the Cc No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi vs . Sh. Bhagwan Dass Page No. 1 Of 12 on 31 August, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62375663/
2 aggrieved and her daughter Manju and has deliberately and intentionally neglected and refused to pay maintenance to the aggrieved and that the aggrieved has no other alternative accommodation for her residence and the respondents have forcefully thrown out her from the share household.
8.

entities.text: Heera Devi vs . Sh. Bhagwan Dass
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has been further averred that the respondent no. 1 is working as Tailor earing Rs. 10000/ per month without any other liability except to maintain the aggrieved which he is not doing despite having sufficient means and income.
It has been also averred that the aggrieved has no independent source of income and is dependent upon her parents and on the mercy of relatives.
Hence the present case.

9. Notice of the applications was issued to respondent who entered appearance through counsel on 11.07.2014 and filed the reply on behalf of respondent no.1 wherein he did not dispute his marriage to the CC No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi Vs. Sh. Bhagwan Dass Page No. 4 of 12 aggrieved but stated that he was aged about 59 years and suffering from various ailments without any source of income and he has denied working as a tailor now.

entities.text: CC No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi Vs. Sh. Bhagwan Dass
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was contended therein that the case had been filed only to harass the respondents as it was a false case.
All allegations of harassment and cruelty have been denied on merits.
He has also stated that the aggrieved shall not be dispossessed from the top floor except in accordance with due process of law.
10. In her replication filed thereto, the aggrieved denied the averments of the respondent no.1 and reaffirmed averments made in her application.
11. Domestic Incident Report was filed by the Protection officer on 30.01.2014.

However as respondent did not file his income affidavit despite numerous opportunities nor joined the proceedings despite repeated calls, he was proceeded exparte on 01.06.2015.
12.

To prove her case, the aggrieved Heera Devi led exparte complainant evidence and examined only herself as CW1 and tendered her evidence by way of affidavit (Ex. CW1/1) on similar lines as her application and also proved the following documents: Copy of Ration Card, Ex.CW1/A (colly. 2 pages); Copy of complaint dt. 15.10.2013 Ex.CW1/B and Copy of complaint dt. 18.10.2013 Ex.CW1/C.
13.
Final arguments were advanced by Sh Yudhister Singh, counsel for the aggrieved.
14. I have given my thoughtful consideration to the submissions made during the course of final arguments and have carefully perused the entire evidence on record.

15. By virtue of Section 2(a), the reliefs under the Protection of Women CC No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi Vs. Sh. Bhagwan Dass Page No. 5 of 12 From Domestic Violence Act, 2005 can be availed by a woman only if she is in a domestic relationship with the respondent and was subjected to domestic violence by the respondent.

entities.text: Protection of Women CC No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi Vs. Sh. Bhagwan Dass Page No. 5 of 12
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
16. The testimony of CW1 in respect of her being married to respondent has not been disputed by the respondent who has rather admitted in his written statement that he got married to the Cc No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi vs . Sh. Bhagwan Dass Page No. 1 Of 12 on 31 August, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62375663/
3 aggrieved in 1980.
Hence, the fact of marriage between aggrieved and respondent no.1 being an admitted fact, the same need not be proved by further evidence.

It is also not in dispute that they were both residing in DII/314, Madangir, New Delhi as husband and wife and thus, from the admissions of the respondent as also her unrebutted oral testimony the aggrieved has proved that she was living with the respondent as wife of the respondent and was living together with him in a shared household / matrimonial home.
Hence the factum of domestic relationship between the aggrieved and the respondent has been proved.
17. In respect of the infliction of the domestic violence, the testimony of CW1 and the documents relied upon by her have gone unrebutted.
Despite opportunities the respondent for reasons best known to him chose not to join the present proceedings to controvert any evidence led by the aggrieved.
Thus the averments of the aggrieved as also her testimony in her evidence by way of affidavit are deemed to be admitted by the respondent as it has remained unchallenged and unrebutted.
Further, no reason has been brought on record to disbelieve the uncontroverted evidence led by the aggrieved.

Accordingly, by unrebutted testimony, the aggrieved has been able to prove that the CC No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi Vs. Sh. Bhagwan Dass Page No. 6 of 12 respondent has committed certain acts of physical and economic violence against the aggrieved and thus, as the aggrieved person has been able to prove the domestic violence committed upon her, she is entitled to claim reliefs under the Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act, 2005 against the respondent.
Reliefs 18. Protection Order Under Section 18 of Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act:

entities.text: CC No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi Vs. Sh. Bhagwan Dass
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act, 2005
entities.label: STATUTE

entities.text: Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Aggrieved has prayed for an protection order by prohibiting respondents from entering the school/college/workplace as also prohibiting from respondent(s) from entering the school/college/any other place of her children; Prohibiting respondents from stopping her from going to her school; Prohibiting alienation of assets by the respondent as also directions against the respondent to stay away from the dependents/relatives/any other person of the aggrieved person to prohibit violence against him and also order against the respondents restraining him from indulging from any of the act of domestic violence act defined under section 2 (g) read with section 3 of the Act.
19.

The entire evidence as led by the aggrieved is silent as to any allegation of domestic violence committed by Respondent by entering in the school/ college/ workplace of the aggrieved or at school/ college/ any other place of her children or in respect of respondent no.1 stopping the aggrieved from stopping her from going to her school.
Rather it is duly noted that no evidence has been brought on record that the aggrieved is going to school/college or has any workplace.

It is also duly noted that CC No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi Vs. Sh. Bhagwan Dass Page No. 7 of 12 the aggrieved has not disclosed the name of the college where her daughter Manju is pursuing her graduation and in the absence of the any college being specified, no blank orders can be passed in favour of aggrieved and against the respondent.

entities.text: CC No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi Vs. Sh. Bhagwan Dass
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the said reliefs are declined as being vague.

Cc No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi vs . Sh. Bhagwan Dass Page No. 1 Of 12 on 31 August, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62375663/
4 20.

entities.text: Heera Devi vs . Sh. Bhagwan Dass
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The aggrieved has also sought prohibition of alienation of assets by the respondent without specifying the assets in question.
Thus, in the absence of sufficient details of the assets having been pleaded by the aggrieved, the protection order as sought is declined as being vague.
21. The aggrieved has also sought directions against the respondent to stay away from the dependents/relatives/any other person of the aggrieved person to prohibit violence against them.
However, no evidence has been led by the aggrieved about her husband having contacted her relatives in any manner and hence, the said relief appears to be vague in nature and hence is declined.

22. However, keeping in view that certain acts of domestic violence have been committed upon the aggrieved in the past which resulted in the present matter, and to further ensure safety and security of the aggrieved, I deem it fit to pass a protection order in favour of the aggrieved thereby restraining the respondent from committing any further acts of domestic violence against the aggrieved until further orders.

Any default in compliance of this order shall entail a liability under Section 31 of Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act.
23. Residence Order Under Section 19 of Protection of Women From CC No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi Vs. Sh. Bhagwan Dass Page No. 8 of 12 Domestic Violence Act:

entities.text: Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act
entities.label: STATUTE

entities.text: Protection of Women From CC No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi Vs. Sh. Bhagwan Dass Page No. 8 of 12
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The aggrieved has prayed for residence orders to the effect that respondent be restrained from dispossessing or throwing her out from the shared household or entering that portion of the shared household in which she resides.
She has further sought orders restraining the respondent from alienating/ disposing/ encumbering the shared household and renouncing their rights in the shared household.
She has further sought order for continued access to her personal effects as the respondent did not allow her to use necessary amenities i.e. bathroom, toilet etc and to go outside the house.
She has further sought that respondent be directed to remove himself from the shared household as also that he should secure same level of alternate accommodation or pay rent for the same.

She has also sought direction against the respondent to vacate the ground floor of the house and to allow the aggrieved to reside in the ground floor peacefully and he be further restrained from dispossessing or throwing her out from the shared household.

24. From her unrebutted testimony, the aggrieved has been able to prove that till 26.10.2013 she was residing at the ground floor of the property DII/314, Madangir, New Delhi and had to vacate the same only due to the domestic violence inflicted upon her.
In his written statement the respondent has asserted his exclusive possession of the first floor without specifying the date thereof.
Thus, it is proved that unrebutted testimony of the aggrieved as well as admissions in the written statement that the ground floor of the said property was the shared household of the aggrieved.
That being so, the aggrieved is entitled to CC No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi Vs. Sh. Bhagwan Dass Page No. 9 of 12 reside therein being the wife of the respondent.

entities.text: CC No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi Vs. Sh. Bhagwan Dass
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, the respondent is directed to allow the aggrieved to reside in the ground floor of the property DII/314, Madangir,
New Delhi till further orders.

The respondent is also restrained from alienating/ disposing/
encumbering the shared household and renouncing his rights in the shared household in any manner so as to defeat the residence order passed in favour of the aggrieved.

Cc No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi vs . Sh. Bhagwan Dass Page No. 1 Of 12 on 31 August, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62375663/
5 25.

entities.text: Heera Devi vs . Sh. Bhagwan Dass
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the residence order as passed in favour of the aggrieved, the other reliefs for residence order are declined as being inconsistent with the awarded relief.

As residence order in respect of the ground floor have been passed, no need remains for passing any orders for continued access to personal effects of the aggrieved or or for securing same level of alternate accommodation or rent for the same or for directing the respondent to remove himself from the shared household or to vacate the ground floor in view of the protection order already having been passed in favour of the aggrieved which sufficiently protect the aggrieved from further incidents of domestic violence.
26. Monetary Reliefs Under Section 20 of Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act:

entities.text: Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The aggrieved has prayed Rs. 5000/ as medical expenses and Rs. 50,000/ as loss of the future prospects of the aggrieved due to mental and physical torture and for the loss due to the respondent restraining her from going to her school.

She has further claimed Rs. 2000/ per month towards towards food, clothes, medications and other basic necessities; Rs. 2000/ per month towards school fees and related expenses for the daughter Manju; Rs. 1000/ per CC No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi Vs. Sh. Bhagwan Dass Page No. 10 of 12 month towards household expenses and Rs. 1000/
towards other expenses.

entities.text: Heera Devi Vs. Sh. Bhagwan Dass
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 27. As per the settled law, the aggrieved as well as her children are entitled to get monetary relief which is adequate, fair, reasonable and consistent with the standard of living to which the aggrieved person is accustomed.
In her evidence CW1/1, the aggrieved has alleged that the respondent is working as a tailor earning Rs. 10,000/ per month.

The fact that the respondent is skilled as a tailor has not been denied by the respondent in his written statement though a stand was taken by him that due to ill health and old age he is no longer working which stand he chose not to prove by not contesting the case.

Thus, the testimony the CW1 goes unrebutted and as the aggrieved is the wife of the respondent without any means of sustaining herself, as also keeping in view that it is the legal duty of the respondent being the husband to maintain his wife, assuming the income of the respondent to be that of a skilled worker as per the Minimum Wages Act i.e. Rs. 10,500/ per month, I deem it fit to award a sum of Rs. 5000/ per month to the aggrieved by the respondent as maintenance for herself.
The amount shall be payable from the date of filing of the petition till further orders.
The daughter Manju being major and thus beyond the purview of the Act, no monetary relief can be awarded towards her by way of this order.

28. Respondent shall pay the said amount directly into the account of the aggrieved upon supplying the details of the bank account within one week from today to the respondent and filing a copy on record.
The CC No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi Vs. Sh. Bhagwan Dass Page No. 11 of 12 amount shall be payable by 10th day of every English calendar month starting from the next month.

entities.text: CC No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi Vs. Sh. Bhagwan Dass
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The arrears be cleared within the period of six months.
29. The default shall be viewed in terms of the judgment of Hon'ble High Court in Gaurav Sondhi Vs. Divya Sondhi-120 DLT(2005)426.

entities.text: Gaurav Sondhi Vs. Divya Sondhi-120 DLT(2005)426.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Any maintenance that may have already been paid or has been awarded by any other forum, shall be accordingly adjusted.
30. Compensation Under Section 22 of Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act:

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
The aggrieved has not led any specific evidence to prove loss of the Rs. 50,000/ to her, hence, the relief Cc No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi vs . Sh. Bhagwan Dass Page No. 1 Of 12 on 31 August, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62375663/
6

entities.text: Heera Devi vs . Sh. Bhagwan Dass
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: as claimed is denied.
31. No grounds exist for granting any other relief in favour of aggrieved.
32. Application of the aggrieved under Section 12 of the Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is accordingly disposed off in the said terms.

As the respondent is exparte, a copy of this order be served upon him through the Protection Officer.
34. File be consigned to the record room after necessary compliance.

28. Respondent shall pay the said amount directly into the account of the aggrieved upon supplying the details of the bank account within one week from today to the respondent and filing a copy on record.
The CC No: 189/1 Smt. Heera Devi Vs. Sh. Bhagwan Dass Page No. 11 of 12 amount shall be payable by 10th day of every English calendar month starting from the next month.
The arrears be cleared within the period of six months.
Any maintenance that may have already been paid or has been awarded by any other forum, shall be accordingly adjusted.
